name: Central bank stress
summary: Markets weigh a large Fed rise in December amid White House pressure; yen near ¥159 per dollar; BoE at 4%
state: Markets weigh a rare 50bp Federal Reserve rise at its December meeting after a third above-forecast CPI print, while President Trump wants cuts (The Edge Malaysia, 17 Nov). The yen traded near ¥159.3 per dollar on 26 Nov, close to the 160 level that prompted intervention in the summer (Yahoo Finance). The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since 2023 (Trading Economics). No emergency move or attempt to remove a central-bank head was found as of 26 Nov.
for_you: Borrowing costs may stay high or rise further; people with variable-rate loans and businesses exposed to the yen or dollar face rate and currency swings.
rubric_hit: Open political pressure on the Fed and a stagflationary dilemma = Watch; no emergency move

sources.title: The Edge Malaysia — Fed weighs larger rate rise as inflation stays high
Trading Economics — BoE raises rates for 1st time since 2023

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
